findings:
Decision question: does stream-only 50% leave chance on pink? NO. Every pink basis stays at chance at 50% (best rG 8.391 / .9% full). The real gains are at 85% and 70%.

1. Global PCA subspace on pink (expected: the stream keeps its content). Happened: the subspace keeps 91% of stream energy at 50% and still gives 9.473 / 0% (quick). Why: energy is not content. The loud dims fill the energy. The readers read the low-energy directions.

2. Reader-weighted basis, no back-map (rG). Happened, full: 85% .955 / 62.7% against coord 1.394 / 55.7% and rand 6.205 / 8.1%. 70%: 3.206 / 25.6% against coord 6.845 / 6.9% and rand 10.688 / .4%. Paired KL rG minus coord: -.439 +- .058 at 85%, -3.638 +- .109 at 70%. At 95% rG ties coord (.230 against .232, agree 82.1 against 82.9). The back-map form 'read' gives 1.048 / 60.7% at 85% and 3.533 / 21.3% at 70%. rG against read is inside the 200-photo noise on quick rows. On full rows rG is ahead by 2.0 and 4.3 agree points.

3. Planted test T+ (one direction u gets 10x the top variance and is removed from every reader). Kept share of u at 85% / 50%: pca 1.000 / 1.000, pcan 1.000 / 1.000, read (C^1/2 back-map) .294 / .195 = FAIL, rsym .107 / .061 = FAIL, rG .000 / .000. rG passes by construction, because G u = 0. So for rG this is only an implementation check. The rand null carries the evidence. The useful result: the back-map form and the symmetrized form fail.

4. Per-site bases with a k x k map on each skip (SliceGPT form, own forward, f = 1 KL 0). On pink it is WORSE than one global basis: 95% 1.552 / 56.5%, 85% 4.734 / 20.0%, 70% 8.853 / 1.0%. The rand per-site null is 12.732 / 0% at 85%. LABELLED PHOTO CHECK (256 held photos in the basis, off the board, quick): 85% .270 / 84.5%, 70% .812 / 70.0%, 50% 2.634 / 35.5%. That is the only row that leaves chance at 50%. On photos the global bases at 50% give pca 6.536 / 7.0% and read 4.655 / 11.5%. Photo coordinates (same fold) give 1.113 / 63.0% at 85% and 10.459 / 0% at 50%. So photos alone with coordinates do not leave chance. Photos AND a per-site subspace do. A 50% subspace can hold the stream content. Pink picks the wrong per-site subspaces.

5. ResNet read maps (full). 85%: 2.380 / 32.3% against the same-form null 3.739 / 17.0% (+15.3 agree, paired -1.359 +- .053). Meanfold is 4.334 / 14.3%. At 95% the map gives .701 / 65.7% and the null .771 / 65.4%. So the 95% gain over meanfold (.897 / 61.2%) is mostly the mean part plus a generic regression. 50% stays at chance (7.657 / .4%). R2 of the cut channels from the kept ones on X is .12-.46 (stem reader .77-.86). A rotated subspace is not possible on ResNet: ReLU acts per channel after the add. The 1x1 map is legal because it folds into the kept columns, so the parameter count stays the same.

Photo use: pink X only in every board row. Held photos only in the labelled check rows (input 'held256-CHECK', scratch.jsonl only). BatchNorm statistics are never read. The ResNet rule edits running_mean as the inference map only.

Paired KL on the 800 photos outside the quick set. The number is the other row minus J, so plus means J is better.
- Stream fold, against off: +.098 +- .007 at 95%, +.883 +- .033 at 85%.
- Stream fold, against its same-form null: +.070 +- .005 at 95%, +.578 +- .025 at 85%.
- Inner fold, against off: +.030 +- .004 at 95%, +.536 +- .022 at 85%.
- Inner fold, against its null: +.012 +- .002 at 95%, +.242 +- .010 at 85%.
- Floor order: -.056 +- .020 at 95%, +.030 +- .048 at 85%.
- P5 null order: +.136 +- .022 at 95%, +.227 +- .044 at 85%.

How to read agree: at 1,000 photos its noise is about 1.6 points at 95% and 1.1 points at 85%. On agree, only the stream fold at 85% clears that noise: +5.2 against off and +4.5 against its null. The order differences (+1.3 / +1.5) are ties. The inner fold against its null (+.3 / +1.7) is a tie on agree.

WHAT ADDS UP
1. The stream fold carries the most. It is a closed-loop regression, front to back, at every reader of a cut stream channel, with a constant unit. It replaces the P6 mean fold.
2. The inner fold adds a smaller real KL gain. Its null reaches 40% of the gain at 95% and 45% at 85%, so a large part is first moment.
3. The two folds add up. At 85% they give .883 and .536 of KL each, against a total of 3.69 from the floor to J.

WHAT OVERLAPS
1. The P5 order. In round 1 it gave +3.7 agree alone. Here it gave +8.5 agree alone (quick: 1.637 / 44.0% against 1.937 / 35.5%). That gain is gone once both folds are on: the floor order is better by .056 KL at 95% and ties at 85%. P5 beats its own null by .136 / .227, but that null harms (alone at full: 1.844 / 41.2% against the floor's 1.665 / 42.7%), so this is not evidence for P5.
2. The P6 mean fold overlaps the inner fold fully. This is QUICK ONLY (200 photos): p5+fold 1.361 / 51.5% and p5+mean+fold 1.343 / 51.5%. Mean against perm inside the joint: 1.343 against 1.349. The stream fold contains the mean fold as its constant, so the two parts never run together.
3. The affine inner fold (constant unit into bn2) ties the plain fold once the stream fold is on. Quick: 1.252 / 54.5% against 1.256 / 54.5%.

Expected / happened / why: I predicted +7 agree at 95%, with the order and the mean fold adding and the inner fold overlapping the mean fold. The result was +12 agree at full, but the parts are different from the prediction. The folds carry the gain and the order does not. Why: the floor's pink-noise order loses mostly first-moment and linear content. A fold of the kept channels can predict that content again, so a better choice of channels matters less after the repair.
